findings.title: Shared-budget test also passes when every repository gets its own budget
findings.body: The test sets a 25ms timeout and four repositories whose `resolveRemoteFunc` blocks until its `remoteCtx` is done. The assertion is `elapsed > 250ms`. If the manager gave each resolution its own 25ms deadline (the behaviour this PR removes), the total would be about 4×25ms = 100ms. That is under the 250ms threshold, so the test would still pass. It does not check what its name says, which is that one budget is shared across resolution. It would catch an unbounded hang, but not a loss of sharing. Make the two cases differ clearly. For example, use a longer per-call timeout (say 200ms) with a threshold below 2× that, or have the fake record the `remoteCtx.Deadline()` of each call and assert all four are equal. Asserting identical deadlines is deterministic and does not depend on timing.
